newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forward dlr premia slip on RBI swap deals.
newsitem.headline: Indian forward dlr premia slip on RBI swap deals.

text.p: Premia fell sharply in the forward market on Wednesday as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) conducted major swap transactions, dealers said.
"RBI was rolling over large swaps maturing in December," said a dealer. "They bought December over May," he said.
"Forwards dropped more than 14 paise," he said.
June dollar premia fell to 1.62/1.66 rupees in late afternoon deals from 1.70/1.74 opening, dealers said.
Premia on other durations also fell accordingly, they said.
Dealers said the size of Wednesday's swap deals was substantial. RBI officials were not immediately available for comment.

RBI also bought spot dollars earlier in the day at 35.75 level, dealers said. RBI's dollar buying, followed by sustained buying by a Calcutta bank, pulled the rupee to 35.80/82 level in latest deals from 35.73/74 opening, dealers said.
